title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 74–77): Grothendieck builds a 'relative differential invariant' C(f,g) for pairs of local étale maps f, g from a complex curve X (analytic) into a 1-dimensional homogeneous space. The space is acted on by a group G. C(f,g) is to be characterised axiomatically by properties a)–e): a cocycle/difference property, invariance under G acting on g, a uniqueness statement (C(f,g)=C(f,h) and g(x)=h(x) imply g=h), and a torsor/surjectivity property. The model case is the Schwarzian derivative, for PGL acting on P^1. Earlier cases: (a) G_a acting on E^1 gives dg−df, or dg/df for étale maps. (b) G_m acting by homotheties. Here a basis section of a line bundle L gives a connection, so L^*/C^* ≅ Conn(L). For L=O this gives g ↦ dg/g, O^*/C^* ≅ ω, and B(f,g) = d(g/f)/(g/f) = dg/g − df/f.

This page continues case b). The aim is a homothety-invariant attached to étale maps g: X → C, which are allowed to have zeros. He tries g ↦ g/dg, a vector field, i.e. a section of ω^{⊗−1}. This is invariant under g ↦ ag, a ∈ C^*. He sets C^!(f,g) = g(dg)^{-1} − f(df)^{-1}. Properties a) (additivity) and c) (invariance C(f,g) = C(f,ag)) hold. Property d) holds only at points that are not zeros, as the deleted clause shows: if g(x)=h(x)=0, then any c·g with suitable c also matches. Property e) fails. The reason is that g/dg is not an arbitrary local section of ω^{−1}: it vanishes exactly at the zeros of g, with linear part 1 there. So the map from E_X is not onto a torsor.

Conclusion: restrict to E_X^* = étale maps into C^* = G_m. These can be sent either to ω^{⊗−1,*} by g/dg, or to ω^* by dg/g. Here ω^* is viewed as an O^*-torsor, and one takes the 'ratio' invariant C^!(f,g) = (dg/g):(df/f) = (dg/df)(g/f) ∈ Γ(X, O_X^*). This is the multiplicative analogue of the previous difference B.

General principle extracted: the method succeeds when the value space is a homogeneous space under the group: P^1(C) under PGL, E^1(C) under G_a, G_m(C) under G_m. The action of C^* on C is not transitive (0 is fixed), hence 'mauvais'.

Then he starts case c): Aff(1) = G_m·G_a acting on E^1. The next page solves this via E_X → ω^* → Conn(ω), giving the pre-Schwarzian D(f,g) = d log(dg/df) = (g''/g' − f''/f')dt. Case d) on the following page treats Aut(G_m)⋉G_m acting on G_m, with values in quadratic differentials (df/f)^2. The whole sequence is an axiomatic 'Klein hierarchy' leading up to the Schwarzian as the invariant for PGL(2) on P^1.
errors: Property d) as first stated is false at zeros of g, h, since the local solutions of g/g' = h/h' through a common zero form a family g = c·h. Grothendieck noticed this, hence the struck-out clause restricting to non-zeros.

Property e) fails for g ↦ g/dg on all of E_X: the image lies in vector fields vanishing exactly at zeros of g with derivative 1. Grothendieck explicitly marks 'faux e' and corrects course by restricting to G_m-valued maps.

Minor: the ratio invariant (dg/g):(df/f) is invariant under g ↦ ag but not under g ↦ 1/g. This is fine here, since inversion is only brought in on the next page (case d), which forces passage to quadratic differentials.

ideas.what: Relative invariant of two charts into a homogeneous space G\Y, valued in a torsor (ω, ω^*, O^*). The hierarchy translation → dg−df; homothety → dg/g−df/f or (dg/g)/(df/f); affine → pre-Schwarzian; projective → Schwarzian.
ideas.modern_name: (G,X)-structures on curves / differential invariants of Klein geometries; pre-Schwarzian and Schwarzian as cocycles
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical: Schwarz, Lie, Cartan. Modern treatments: Gunning (projective structures, 1960s); Deligne (1970) for projective connections; Ovsienko–Tabachnikov for the hierarchy.
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as such; the Schwarzian and projective structures are treated in Deligne, LNM 163 (1970).

ideas.what: Criterion: the construction works iff the target is a homogeneous space under the group; a non-transitive action (C^* on C) fails.
Basis sheaf L^* as an O^*-torsor; L^*/C^* ≅ Conn(L), and ω^* treated as an O^*-torsor.
ideas.modern_name: Logarithmic derivative / connection attached to a trivialisation

deep.surprise_reason: A careful heuristic exploration of how to axiomatise differential invariants (warm-up cases before the Schwarzian), including a self-corrected failed attempt. The 'homogeneous space = condition of success' principle is pleasant but classical (G,X)-structure theory; nothing here appears new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'Si on veut par contre une invariance en ℰ_X^*' (or 'ℰ_X'), not 'Si on veut pas créer une invariance'.
'Mieux [?] g(dg)^{-1} ne va être id. une ...' is probably a parenthetical '(car g(dg)^{-1} ne va pas être ... si g ∈ Γℰ_X !)' explaining why e) fails; the exact words are uncertain.
'Et_{C-an}(X, G_m^*)' is probably 'Ét_{C-an}(X, C^*)', i.e. étale analytic maps into C^*.
'PGl(1)' is as written; it means the projective group of P^1 (i.e. PGL(2)) in Grothendieck's indexing.
'C^!(f,g) = C^!(·, ag)' should read 'C^!(f,g) = C^!(f, ag)'.
